title: Maven build cache + setup-java cache interaction causes stale JARs in ~/.m2/repository
description:
When runAlways was removed for maven-install-plugin (#847), a subtle interaction between two CI caches caused stale JARs:

1. setup-java caches ~/.m2/repository keyed by pom.xml hash — persists across many commits
2. Maven build cache skips install phase when source is unchanged — stale JARs in ~/.m2/repository never get overwritten
3. compute_module_classpath resolves reactor modules from ~/.m2/repository JARs, not target/classes

This caused NoSuchMethodError for peekNextId() added in #851 but called unconditionally in #853.

The immediate fix (re-adding runAlways) costs ~30s per build. Better solutions to explore:

- **Different caching for CI vs local**: Local builds can aggressively cache since ~/.m2/repository is always warm. CI needs runAlways because setup-java cache is stale.
- **Change compute_module_classpath to use target/classes**: Instead of resolving reactor modules from ~/.m2/repository JARs, detect local modules and use their target/classes directories. This makes runtime classpath match compile-time classpath.
- **Per-worktree Maven repository**: Copy ~/.m2/repository into worktree-local storage on worktree creation instead of sharing caches across worktrees. Avoids cross-worktree contamination.
- **Bust setup-java cache on source changes**: Include a source hash in the setup-java cache key so it's invalidated when Java source changes.

The target/classes approach is probably the cleanest — it removes the dependency on ~/.m2/repository for local modules entirely.
